summary: Brought node1's unconfigured vtnet2 (facing lan-b, bridged to node3's enp8s0) into service as a new OPNsense zone "lanb" with static IP 10.60.60.1/24, added a firewall pass rule for the lanb network, and configured node3's enp8s0 as 10.60.60.12/24 via nmcli. Verified node3 reaches node1 on lan-b and reaches node2 (10.100.217.11, on lan-a) through node1's routing/automatic outbound NAT, without breaking the existing SSH management path. Then performed the mandatory rolling restart of node1, node2, and node3 one at a time, proving changed boot identity on each and confirming the lanb interface, firewall rule, node3's static address, and full end-to-end reachability all survived reboot.
actions_performed: Inspected interfaces on node1 (OPNsense), node2, node3 to map physical topology
Used temporary ifconfig/ip addr probes + tcpdump on node1 to determine vtnet2<->node3:enp8s0 and vtnet1<->node2:enp8s0 bridging, then reverted the probes
Edited /conf/config.xml on node1 via Python/ElementTree to add a new 'lanb' interface on vtnet2 with static IP 10.60.60.1/24, backing up config.xml first
Added a firewall pass rule for the lanb network in config.xml
Applied config via `configctl interface reconfigure lanb` and `configctl filter reload`, confirming SSH management access stayed intact
Verified pf ruleset shows the lanb pass rule and automatic outbound NAT covering vtnet2->vtnet0
Configured node3's enp8s0 with static 10.60.60.12/24 persistently via nmcli (RHEL9/NetworkManager)
Verified node3 pings node1 (10.60.60.1) on lan-b and node2 (10.100.217.11) on lan-a through node1
Captured baseline boot identities (kern.boottime on node1, /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id on node2/node3)

Restarted node1, node2, node3 sequentially (one at a time) via native reboot, polled until exec access returned, and confirmed changed boot identity plus recovered config/connectivity for each before moving to the next node

evidence.requirement: node1's lan-b-facing interface (vtnet2) brought into service as its own zone with an address
evidence.summary: config.xml edited to add 'lanb' interface on vtnet2 (10.60.60.1/24), applied via configctl interface reconfigure + filter reload; pfctl shows the lanb pass rule active and vtnet2 covered by outbound NAT
node3's enp8s0 set to 10.60.60.12/24 via nmcli; ping from node3 to 10.60.60.1 succeeds (0% loss)

evidence.requirement: node3 reaches node2 on lan-a through node1
evidence.summary: ping from node3 to node2's lan-a address 10.100.217.11 succeeds (0% loss), routed via node1

evidence.requirement: SSH management path preserved when applying OPNsense filter changes
evidence.summary: configctl filter reload returned OK and subsequent exec commands over SSH continued to succeed; pf ruleset still shows the vtnet0 SSH pass rule intact

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered config/connectivity
evidence.summary: Baseline kern.boottime captured (17:18:37); reboot acked before disconnect; post-restart kern.boottime changed to 17:22:53; lanb interface and pf pass rule confirmed intact after reboot

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered connectivity
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 31949c21...; restart issued; new boot_id 701be57e... confirms reboot; enp1s0 address recovered and ping to node1 (10.100.217.10) succeeds

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered lan-b config and end-to-end connectivity
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 9feeb0bb...; restart issued; new boot_id 91d01ec7... confirms reboot; enp8s0 static IP persisted, and post-restart pings to both node1 (lan-b) and node2 (lan-a via node1) succeed
